R101.note: mongoose.sanitizeFilter() applied to the whole filter correctly neutralizes $-operator injection from extraCriteria while leaving scalar values (including legitimate extra match criteria) untouched.

R102.note: path.basename() strips directory components before the require() call, correctly scoping loads to ./plugins/; simple plugin names pass through unchanged.

R103.note: Switching to [HttpPost] closes link/img-based GET CSRF but the explanation's claim that ASP.NET Core validates anti-forgery tokens automatically on POST for a plain Controller is wrong (needs an explicit [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] or global AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute, neither present), so cross-site auto-submitting form CSRF remains open; verb change itself is the intended, disclosed fix and doesn't harm legitimate use.

R104.note: Moves username into the {0}/{1} filterArgs placeholder array so JNDI escapes it per RFC 2254; correct standard LDAP-injection fix, rest of logic unchanged.

R105.note: Length check (username_len+1+action_len >= 64) correctly rejects oversized input before strcpy/strcat and matches the stated contract exactly, off-by-one verified correct.

R106.note: Standard mysqli prepared statement with bound parameter; null/array return contract preserved.

R107.note: Whitelist validation against known columns closes ${sort} injection while keeping tenantId bound and created_at default; contract explicitly calls for rejecting non-whitelisted values so the added restriction is required, not extraneous.

R108.note: Extension is now taken from the content-detected file-type result instead of client-supplied originalname; correct fix for the sink, no other behavior change.

R109.note: htmlspecialchars(..., ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') applied at the point of HTML concatenation; correct, standard XSS fix with no other change.

R110.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before the write, following the function's existing early-return pattern for invalid input; no legitimate channel (0-7) is rejected.

R111.note: Replacing manual docmd() concatenation with smtp.sendmail() routes addresses through smtplib.putcmd(), which was confirmed by inspecting the installed Python 3.13 stdlib source to raise ValueError on embedded CR/LF; message body and termination behavior preserved (sendmail handles DATA termination itself).

R112.note: id = ANY($1) with the ids array bound as a parameter is the standard safe replacement for a joined IN(...) clause; matches the stated contract, no legitimate id set is rejected.

R113.note: pathinfo(...,PATHINFO_EXTENSION) closes the 'safe-extension-then-dangerous-extension' pattern (e.g. shell.jpg.php) but the destination path still stores the full untouched $originalName, so the exact attack string the write-up's own Verdict names (shell.php.jpg) still has final extension 'jpg' and passes both before and after the fix - the write-up's claim that its fix blocks that example is incorrect.

R114.note: resize(count) correctly makes the packet[i] write safe, but the contract also requires rejecting/reporting counts larger than fields.size(); the fix adds no such check, so fields[i] remains an unchecked out-of-bounds read for oversized count, and this gap is not mentioned anywhere in the write-up.

R115.note: Self-injection via @Lazy InvoiceService and routing the call through self.deleteInvoice() is the standard, correct Spring idiom for restoring proxy-enforced @PreAuthorize on self-invocation; matches the finding's intended behavior.

R116.note: Replacing the string-built setTimeout argument with an arrow-function closure over reminderId/message is the canonical fix; recordReminder receives the same values as before.
